newsitem.title: USA: Japan needs deregulation to grow--spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Japan needs deregulation to grow--spokesman.

text.p: Japan is "sincere" in its efforts to deregulate its economy, without which the country cannot grow on a sustained basis, a Japanese official spokesman said.
"Unless we succeed on this, sustainable economic growth will not be the case," said Hiroshi Hashimoto, spokesman for the Japanese delegation at the Group of Seven summit here.

Japan this week agreed to allow the U.S. to participate in future discussions on deregulating key sectors of the Japanese economy, in a move Washington hopes will reduce the growing trade imbalance between the two countries.
U.S. President Bill Clinton on Thursday voiced concern over Japan's rising bilateral trade surplus in a meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
Japanese officials say the rise is a "cyclical" phenomenon, prompting some observers to question Japan's resolve to fully open its markets.
Yet Hiroshi Hashimoto asserted that Japan is committed to reform.
"We are very much sincere in dealing with deregulation," Hashimoto, the Japanese spokesman, said.
